happened: DOJ's immigration courts issued several rules in 2025-2026. They cut the Board of Immigration Appeals to 15 members (April 2025), let a 2020 Trump-era rule on public-health asylum bars take effect Dec 31, 2025, and made Board review of appeals discretionary (February 2026). In July 2026 DOJ proposed letting immigration judges fine people for contempt.

key_dates.event: Interim rule reduces the Board of Immigration Appeals to 15 members.
2020 public-health asylum bar rule takes effect.
Interim rule on Board appellate procedures.

legal: I did not research lawsuits over these specific rules.
closeness: Some Trump-era rules were revived, but I found no reissuing of every Trump-era immigration court rule. Several rules are new rather than reissued.
uncertain: Whether other 2019-2020 rules (such as those on case delays) were reissued, and whether any of these rules face court challenges.

happened: The July 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) gave the Justice Department $3.33 billion, including money to hire immigration judges and staff, and capped the judge corps at 800 from November 2028. The immigration court system also used temporary immigration judges. In May 2026 it swore in 77 permanent and 5 temporary judges, its largest class, bringing the corps to nearly 700.

key_dates.event: P.L. 119-21 signed, funding immigration judge hiring.
Rule allowing temporary immigration judges published.
77 immigration judges and 5 temporary judges sworn in.

legal: I found no court ruling blocking the hiring.
closeness: More resources went to immigration courts, as recommended. I did not confirm how many of these resources went to cases under the "Remain in Mexico" program, which the recommendation named as an example.
uncertain: How the money is split between immigration courts and other uses in the same section of the law, and how many judges left during the same period. Newest source is from May 2026.

happened: In May 2025, the Justice Department asked a federal judge to end the Flores settlement, which sets rules for holding migrant children. Judge Dolly Gee denied the request in August 2025.

key_dates.event: DOJ asks court to end Flores.
Judge denies the request.
Ninth Circuit hears the government's appeal.

legal: U.S. District Court for the Central District of California (Judge Dolly Gee) denied the motion to terminate the settlement on August 15, 2025. The government appealed; the Ninth Circuit heard argument on June 2, 2026 (Flores v. Blanche, No. 25-6308). I found no appeals ruling yet.
closeness: Direct match: DOJ litigated to end Flores, and the court refused. Same action as ch14-099.
uncertain: The Ninth Circuit has not ruled as far as I found; reports said the panel seemed skeptical of the government's arguments. Newest source is from June 2026.

happened: The Civil Rights Division brought a series of cases in 2026 over hiring that favored temporary visa holders over U.S. workers. It sued Cloudera in April 2026, reached a $3.2 million settlement with OpenAI in August 2026, and announced a $5 million joint settlement with Instacart and the EEOC in October 2026.

key_dates.event: Civil Rights Division sues Cloudera.
Settlement with OpenAI announced.
Joint settlement with Instacart announced.

legal: These were settlements and a lawsuit brought by the government; I did not find rulings against the program.
closeness: Matches the recommendation: active enforcement against hiring that favors foreign or temporary workers over U.S. citizens.
uncertain: How the number of cases compares with earlier years. Newest source is from October 2026.

happened: On February 5, 2025, the Acting Director of the Executive Office for Immigration Review issued a memo (PM 25-19) to re-establish its Anti-Fraud Program. It told staff to report fraud and cooperate with the program and with EOIR's attorney discipline office, and it covers fraud by attorneys and accredited representatives. In July 2026, DOJ proposed a rule letting immigration judges fine people for contempt.

key_dates.event: EOIR memo PM 25-19 re-establishes the Anti-Fraud Program.
EOIR publishes a fact sheet on its Fraud and Abuse Prevention Program.
DOJ proposes civil money penalties for contempt of an immigration judge.

legal: I found no court ruling on the memo.
closeness: Same idea and mechanism: a stronger anti-fraud program in the immigration courts. The memo's main focus is asylum fraud, with attorney fraud as one part, while the chapter put attorney fraud first.
uncertain: How many fraud referrals or attorney discipline cases followed was not checked. The contempt penalty rule was still a proposal as of the newest source (July 2026).

happened: On Feb 5, 2025, the Attorney General ordered all Justice Department offices to end DEI programs and diversity hiring targets, rescind guidance allowing race- or sex-based preferences, and report by March 15, 2025 on DEI positions, programs and contracts. The memo says department decisions, including employment, should avoid identity-based considerations.

key_dates.event: AG memo "Eliminating Internal Discriminatory Practices."

legal: I found no court ruling on this memo.
closeness: Covers the race and sex part of the recommendation. I found no published review of career hiring across all offices for ideology or political views, which the recommendation also asked for.
uncertain: Whether the component reports were finished or made public. Source is from February 2025.

happened: In March 2025 a Deputy Attorney General memo proposed combining several Justice Department units, including the DEA and ATF and some policy offices, according to the Associated Press. In June 2026 the department briefed stakeholders on a plan to merge its three grant offices (OJP, COPS and OVW) into one Bureau of Justice Grants, with a shared office providing human resources, contracting, building support, IT and legal services. As of September 2026 the department said leadership would decide next steps.

key_dates.event: Restructuring memo proposes combining DOJ components.
DOJ briefs stakeholders on a Bureau of Justice Grants.

legal: I found no court case. Some lawmakers say the grants merger conflicts with directions from Congress.
closeness: The grants plan would combine support functions such as HR, IT and legal services, as the chapter suggests, but only for the three grant offices, and it is not final. Public relations is not listed.
uncertain: No merger had been completed as of the department's September 2, 2026 update, and no effective date was given. Whether support functions were combined elsewhere in DOJ was not found.

happened: On April 22, 2025, DOJ ended about 365 Office of Justice Programs grants, worth about $811 million when awarded, saying they did not match its funding priorities. The canceled areas included research, data collection and innovation projects. The Bureau of Justice Statistics kept running core data programs such as its National Prisoner Statistics survey.

key_dates.event: DOJ terminates about 365 Office of Justice Programs grants.

legal: Court challenges to the grant terminations were not checked here.
closeness: Only the general direction matches. I found no DOJ policy telling the Bureau of Justice Statistics to limit itself to core statistics or to stop publishing contractor reports.
uncertain: I could not confirm from a source I opened how much of the cut came from National Institute of Justice research grants, or whether BJS changed which reports it publishes. Newest source is from 2025.

happened: The Bureau of Justice Statistics kept running the National Crime Victimization Survey, moved fully to a redesigned version in January 2025, and renewed its data collection approvals in 2025. In October 2026 the Justice Department released 2025 survey estimates showing violent crime fell.

key_dates.event: Redesigned survey fully in use.
